synopsis: The corpus treats UNECE virtual-testing rules as on-road precedents, not direct off-road approval routes: NATM and DCAS require adaptation, and off-road simulation should provide coverage and design evidence qualified against physical tests [f7545, f5112, f2143]. R171 permits virtual testing for hard-to-reproduce scenarios only after rigorous toolchain credibility evaluation, with the Annex 5 assessment supplied to the Type Approval Authority; dSPACE reports that WP.29 added virtual testing at the end of 2024 [f1217, f2488, f1276]. NATM combines simulation with scenario catalogues, track and real-world tests, audit and in-service monitoring; credibility assessment defines the tool's usable envelope, while physical testing remains necessary [f9743, f9745, f10330]. WP.29 adopted R152 virtual-testing supplements in 2025, but the text dated 28 August 2025 leaves physical confirmation-test numbers to manufacturer–authority agreement, unlike the 30% minimum reported in a working document; January 2024 criticism had identified unresolved credibility issues [f7546, f7549, f7547, f7144]. R152's 5.0 m/s² threshold is a minimum braking demand, not measured deceleration, creating tension with glossary wording that calls it deceleration; R131 and R152 also permit conscious driver interruption of emergency braking [f5993, f6307, f13632, f6323]. The booklet proposes transferring R159-style small-cylinder geometry into machine digital twins for coverage and blind-zone analysis, but the reported 50 mm cylinder dimension was not confirmed against the regulation text [f15220, f5603, f5356].
